title: Three Verb Classifier
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: xAPI
Learning Analytics
xAPI Verbs
Producer Contract
Evidence
description: A p5.js drag-to-bin classifier in which learners sort twelve scripted learner events from a mock Bouncing Ball MicroSim into answered, experienced, interacted or no statement, with feedback on object type, required result field and reasoning, plus the xAPI 1.0.3 JSON of each statement.
audience: Teachers, instructional designers, learning-technology developers and learning-analytics practitioners (college undergraduate and professional development)

educational.topic: The three MicroSim verbs: answered, experienced and interacted
learningObjectives: The learner will classify learner actions in a described MicroSim into the correct verb, object type and required result field, and explain any action that needs no statement.
prerequisites: The five parts of an xAPI statement (Chapter 16)
The three MicroSim verbs and four object types (Chapter 16)

accessibility.notes: Bin buttons and keys 1-4 place the card without dragging; N advances, S shows the statement; feedback uses words as well as color

controls.label: Event card
controls.purpose: Drag into a bin to classify the event

controls.label: Show statement
controls.purpose: Render the statement's verb, object and result as JSON

controls.label: Try again
controls.purpose: Reshuffle the twelve events and reset the score

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Classification practice with rule-based corrective feedback
pedagogical.interactionPattern: Drag-to-bin sorting (concept classifier) with statement preview
keyQuestions: Can this event say whether the learner was right or wrong?
Did time pass in a run, and was the run longer than 250 ms?
Was a control touched on purpose, or was the pointer only crossing it?
commonMisconceptions: A slider movement needs a success or a duration
Only the final correct answer should be recorded
Every pointer movement over a node is evidence
assessmentOpportunities: Naming the required result field for each verb
Explaining the rule that suppresses each no-statement event
